title: Coordinator playbook for cross-team canary rituals (working notes)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note is a lightweight playbook for the person coordinating cross-functional canary activations and A/B rollouts (the "Canary Coordinator"). It collects the ceremony, communication templates, minimum gating metrics, and escalation paths we should use when multiple teams are involved (product, serving runtime, SRE, security, console/observability).

Status and intent:
- Working doc / ritual draft (in_review).
- Goal: reduce coordination overhead and ambiguous responsibilities during progressive exposures.
- Focus on mid-size features that touch runtime, model serving, and console behavior (where traffic partitioning + fallbacks matter).

High-level responsibilities of the Canary Coordinator:
- Own the pre-activation checklist and scheduling (not technical rollout execution).
- Ensure slice owners and on-call contacts are available during activation window.
- Triage first-line alerts and escalate to technical owners per runbook.
- Drive the post-canary retro and capture signal regressions + followups.

Before activation (72–24 hours):
1) Confirm stakeholders and backups
   - Primary: Product PM (feature), Eng owner (feature), Runtime owner, SRE on-call, Observability engineer, Security reviewer.
   - Backup list (secondary owners) and pager rotation for the activation day.
2) Document experiment metadata in one line (for audit)
   - Name: <team>-<feature>-canary-YYYYMMDD
   - Hypothesis: short statement of user/business expectation
   - Primary metric(s): e.g., token latency P95, generate success rate, error-rate, cost-per-request
   - Guardrail metrics: 5xxs, auth errors, egress spikes, quota breaches
3) Create the Slack announcement + pinned checklist in #prod-rollouts (template below).
4) Verify telemetry dashboards and alert thresholds are live in the run window. If instrumentation missing -> postpone.
5) Schedule a short pre-launch sync (15 minutes) to confirm traffic slice assignment and visibility windows.

Activation ceremony (day of):
- Timeboxed windows: prefer 2–4 hour initial windows (overnight windows only for low-exposure features).
- Start with a micro-slice (0.5–1% traffic) for 15–30 minutes, then step to 5% for 30–60 minutes, then 20% if green.
- Default step timings and step sizes should be adjustable by feature risk profile (see risk table).

Quick Slack announcement template (post by coordinator):
"Starting canary: <feature> | slice 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% | lead: <eng> | runbook: <link> | check-in in 30m"

Minimum telemetry and gating (must be green before next step):
- Latency: P95 tokenization/generation latency not up > +30% from baseline.
- Error rate: 5xxs or uncaught failures not > 2x baseline OR absolute > 0.5% (whichever is lower).
- Quality signal (if available): hallucination/regression score not worse than baseline by > 5 points on curated evaluation set.
- Cost signal: cost-per-1k tokens within expected model variant delta (if a more expensive model is used, confirm billing alerts).
- Capacity: GPU utilization below 85% sustained for 5m on the serving pool; queue depth stable.
- Security/PII: no uptick in blocked requests or data-exfiltration alerts.

Automated vs manual gating:
- Automated gates: basic infra alerts (5xx spike, node OOM, average queue depth) auto-revert.
- Manual gates: quality regressions, SLO drifts, or security concerns require coordinator + owner signoff to proceed or rollback.

Rollback rules (escalation):
- Auto-revert triggers should be clear and documented in the runtime config (e.g., "revert on >0.5% 5xxs sustained for 2m").
- Manual rollback initiated by the coordinator if manual gate breaches are confirmed.
- If rollback happens, open a Jira ticket immediately: COPY TEMPLATE: "<feature> canary rollback <YYYYMMDD>" and tag leads.

Roles and contact matrix (example):
- Canary Coordinator: Aisha Patel (owns ceremony + comms)
- Runtime / Serving owner: Diego Ramirez (in-charge of model variants, routing)
- Observability lead: Maya Chen (dashboards + alerts)
- SRE on-call: rotation (pager duty)
- Product PM: Jonah Lee (feature owner, hypothesis)
- Security reviewer: Priya Nair (compliance blocker)

Post-canary ritual and artifacting:
- Immediately after final step: 15-minute post-check (coordinator) to confirm system stability.
- Within 24 hours: short retro note in the rollout doc: outcomes, metrics, anomalies, follow-ups.
- Required artifacts: canary slack thread, dashboard snapshots, logs/incident ids (if any), regression evals.
- If metrics show subtle degradation (not rollback-worthy), assign an investigation ticket with SLO owner and set priority.

Risk classification (quick heuristic):
- Low: UI-only changes, no model swap, no infra dependency.
- Medium: model config change that may affect latency/cost or small runtime flags.
- High: model architecture swap, quantization profile changes, cross-region routing changes, or anything touching private deployment network config.

Step-sizing guidance by risk:
- Low: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% (short waits between steps)
- Medium: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 30% (longer observation windows)
- High: gated manual approvals at each step; consider A/B controls and stronger telemetry including offline evals

Ceremony cadence and meetings:
- Pre-launch sync (15m) the day before or 2 hours before activation (depending on risk).
- Kickoff check-in at start of canary (5m).
- Mid-run check-ins after each step (as needed).
- Post-canary retro (30m) within 48h.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who signs final "go to 100%" for cross-account private deployments? (SLA / security checklist)
- Should we build a simple web UI for coordinators to batch-create canary metadata and kick off Slack threads?
- Do we want a default canary SQL query to surface affected customers per slice? (helps CS)

Examples and templates (copy for quick use):
- Slack: see template above.
- Jira title: "Canary run: <feature> — <date> — <result>"
- Post-mortem tags: canary, rollback, model-regression, perf-degradation

Notes to self / shorthand during runs:
- "watch P95, 5xx, queue depth, hallucination-score, gpu%"
- "if two signals degrade at once -> urgent page SRE + runtime"
- "keep CS on standby if customer-facing changes might affect billing or quotas"

References and linked resources:
- Confluence rollout framework (linked above)
- Runtime auto-revert config docs (PR#4321)
- Previous canary retros: PROD-1287

Revision log:
- 2025-11-05 initial draft by Aisha (skeleton + templates)
- 2025-11-20 added gating thresholds and risk table (Maya)
- 2025-12-02 harmonized with SRE auto-revert settings (Diego)

End of doc.

(Immediate next steps: ping SRE rotation and schedule pre-launch 2 hours before the next A/B run for recommendation validation.)
